initial-default-hoist.extract:
Hoisting only the default continuation calculation
while preserving its complete 625-successor order produced all 17 baseline
moments bit for bit and reduced DE/RE runtime from about 792/1258 seconds to
305/611 seconds on the same machine.
initial-default-hoist.supplementary_source: Real Credit Cycles Fortran optimization audit, 2026-09-01, What changed items 1 and 2: original 36-thread setting and hoist outside the 900-state endogenous loop.
initial-default-hoist.identity_note: The hash identifies the source record; it is not numerical-validation evidence.

early-refactor-history.extract:
## What changed

1. The released `omp_set_num_threads(36)` call was removed. Runtime allocation
   now comes from `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, preventing severe oversubscription on an
   eight-core host.
2. The default continuation value, which depends only on the exogenous state,
   was moved outside the 900-state endogenous loop. This also removes a shared
   OpenMP write race while retaining the released 625-term summation order.
3. Continuation expectations that depend only on `(exogenous state, candidate
   action)` are computed once per policy update instead of once for every
   current endogenous state.
4. The approximate cached objective identifies every action within `1e-12` of
   the maximum. For only that tied top set, dividends are recomputed and the
   25 nonzero successor additions are performed in exactly the author order.
   The successor loop is outermost and tied actions are inner, preserving each
   scalar addition sequence while exposing vectorizable work. The approximate
   scan stores continuation and price arrays with candidate action as the
   contiguous dimension.
5. Simulation forecast loops visit the 25 nonzero transition successors, not
   all 625 possible successors.
6. The redundant final distribution call is skipped when policy iteration has
   already produced the final distribution. The `doVFI=0` path keeps it.
7. Payout terms are factorized into current-state, capital-action, and
   debt-adjustment caches. A contiguous 900-by-900 action-cost table removes
   repeated indirect indexing. This table is used only for the guarded
   approximate scan; final tied candidates retain the released formula.
8. The build uses `-funroll-loops`; separate DE and RE executions restore every
   baseline output bit while reducing wall time relative to otherwise identical
   `-O3` builds.
9. Stage timers and command-line evaluators make policy solution, simulation,
   raw Q, penalized `fGMM`, and the complete moment vector observable.

re-interval-history.extract:
A subsequent cold batch evaluated all 28 stored RE parameter rows with the
tracked interval-guard binary. It executed 28 unique candidates with no cache
hits in `1902.492909` seconds, or `67.946175` seconds per row. Every one of the
476 moment cells was bitwise equal to the author-package stored moments; all 28
rows were fully equal. Raw Q recomputed by the candidate differed from Q
recomputed from stored moments by at most `3.47e-17`, and top-1/3/5/10 ranking
was unchanged. The calibration-report SHA-256 is
`18291eaf0f27f96c5fabfba3395bfa4114d12a0abb64dcad476149a8ca11a5b0`.

de-interval-history.extract:
The isolated wrapper-literal published evaluation executed in the 2026-09-01
rescue turn. It took `77.885571` seconds, versus `178.826807` seconds for the
separately stored conservative-exact execution of the same complete parameter
vector, a `2.296x` wall-time improvement. All 17 model moments were bitwise
equal and raw sixteen-moment Q was `0.15327348165047086` in both paths.

Four additional sequential evaluations used author-package rows 1, 2, 15, and
31. Their 68 moment cells were bitwise equal to the package's stored moments;
their four raw Q values were bitwise equal to the existing full-screen Fortran
calibration of those rows. This includes row 15, the pre-existing
`eta_k+2%` perturbation with Q `0.14448559046953308`. The four-point thermal
load run took `533.394672` seconds in total; its per-row times ranged from
`92.094891` to `153.476182` seconds, so it is fidelity evidence rather than a
clean performance benchmark.

Across the wrapper point and these four stored rows, the interval profile made
291 policy updates. Its exact shortlist averaged `3.754509` actions out of 900,
had a maximum of 29, and invoked no full-action fallback. The complete finite
comparison is therefore 85 of 85 moment cells bitwise equal and five of five Q
values bitwise equal to their declared Fortran comparators. A fresh NumPy
matrix product differs by one last bit on three stored rows because it uses a
different accumulation path; it is not the bitwise-Q comparator.

simulation-pruning-history.extract:
The source dependency is exact. Firm-level moments use `t=51,...,56`; their
largest lead is `t+2`, so firm-specific states and outcomes are required only
through period 58. Aggregate distribution dynamics still run through the full
302-period path. The published macro-moment code uses `t=50,...,300`, or 251
observations, notwithstanding the `Tgood=250` parameter name. The SMM-only
aggregate loop retains only the three series that enter the model-moment
vector: author `Ysim`, default frequency, and mean spread. Their state-loop and
scalar addition orders are unchanged. Capital, investment, bond-return,
spread-histogram, BAA-spread, MPK-dispersion, aggregate-profit forecast-error,
and firm-median-spread diagnostics are omitted; the resulting profile must not
be used to request those author diagnostic outputs.

All material executions from this experiment are reported below. The
sequential full-batch timing comparisons are intentionally not interpreted as
causal speed measurements because the unchanged policy stage moved with host
temperature and scheduling.

| Execution family | Evaluations | Numerical result | Timing result and role |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 25-state interval-guard, four rows, old then micro-58 | 4 old + 4 new | 68/68 moment cells and four raw Q values bitwise equal; output moment and objective files byte-equal | 8.143 s old versus 8.147 s new; simulation sums 0.990 versus 0.962 s; too small for an adoption claim |
| 25-state interval-guard, full 28 rows, sequential | 28 old + 28 new | 476/476 moment cells and all 28 raw Q values bitwise equal | 74.638 s old versus 116.649 s new, while unchanged policy time also moved from 61.796 to 98.530 s; thermal/scheduling contamination, no causal performance result |
| optimized envelope, four-row ABBA micro-58 check | 8 old + 8 new | all repeated moments and Q values bitwise equal | aggregate simulation time 2.042 s old versus 1.879 s new; aggregate wall time 7.927 versus 7.576 s; positive but short-run evidence |
| optimized envelope, SMM-only four-row bracket | 4 old + 8 new | all 204 returned moment cells and 12 Q values agree with their repeated candidates | 3.749 s new, 6.048 s old, then 5.827 s new; host transitioned during the bracket, so only numerical parity is retained |
| optimized envelope, SMM-only full 28 rows | 28 new, compared with the existing live-identity 28-row artifact | 476/476 moment cells, all 28 raw Q values, parameters, and complete rank order bitwise equal; fixed inputs, driver, controls, candidate IDs, live old binary, and live old solver identity were checked | current new batch 49.908 s with 11.182 s simulation and 32.893 s policy; the older artifact was 31.025 s, so cross-time totals are not a speed comparison |
| one-point alternating transition sequence | 8 old + 8 new | every 17-moment vector and Q bitwise equal | overall simulation means 0.3475 and 0.3472 s; a mid-sequence host transition makes the pooled timing uninformative |
| one-point hot-host ABBA sequence | 12 old + 12 new | every 17-moment vector and Q bitwise equal | simulation median 0.4345 s old versus 0.3936 s new, a 9.4% stage reduction; wall medians also moved, but the unchanged policy stage moved too |

The strongest performance claim supported by these runs is therefore narrow:
the retained simulation stage is about 9 percent faster on the stabilized hot
host. Applying that reduction to the earlier fast batch, where simulation was
7.858 of 31.025 seconds, projects only about a 2.4 percent total reduction, or
roughly a 1.024x end-to-end speedup. The profile is implemented and fully
calibrated over the stored rows but remains optional and default-off because
the CPU gain is modest.
